title: Book Three · Chapter 44: The Sixth Letter Goes
story:
On Friday, Ronan finishes the letter with his new pen.

He has already written about the run and his birthday. Now he adds the summer part.

We will be here in the holiday. Tell me the dates when you know them. Kai wants to meet you. Anna does too.

He stops at Anna's name. He has not asked her yet.

Ronan draws one neat line through those three words. He does not change the rest.

At school, he finds Anna beside the window. She is looking at a drawing of the hall door.

“Leo may come in the holiday,” he says.

“You told me. Does he know when?”

“Not yet. Would you like to meet him?”

“Yes. Tell me the days. I have some plans with my friend too.”

She turns the drawing toward him. There is a new window at one side.

“We want to look at more buildings. The little museum, maybe.”

“For the pictures?”

“For the rooms too.”

Ronan looks at the space beside the new window. Then Kai comes over and asks about the football after lunch.

“Leo may come back,” Ronan tells him.

“Good. Can he kick the ball?”

“Usually.”

“Then tell him to bring his feet.”

Anna laughs. She puts her drawing away, and the three of them get ready for the lesson.

After school, Ronan reads his letter again at home. He adds another line below the crossed-out words.

I asked Anna today. She would like to meet you. We need the dates first.

Mum is at the table with a customer. Ronan waits near the shelf until they finish looking at a sleeve.

“Can Leo stay here?” he asks after the woman leaves.

Mum looks around their room.

“Where would he sleep?”

Ronan looks too. There is little space between the beds and the table.

“I don't know.”

“Ask about his family's plans first. We can offer a meal. A bed is another thing.”

He nods. He adds one final question about the place Leo will stay.

He writes that Mum and Dad still have work in the holiday. A dinner needs a free evening.

Then he folds the letter and puts it in an envelope. The new pen leaves his fingers clean. He checks its cap before he puts it away.

At the post office, he buys a stamp and sends the sixth letter.

On his way home, the air feels warm against his face. There is still school work tonight and a whole part of spring before the holiday.

He passes the tool shop and sees two boys study the little parts in its window. One has a ball under his arm.

This time, Ronan knows his name. He lifts a hand, and Kai turns to call him over.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

neat＝整齐的；crossed-out＝划掉的；offer＝提出提供；cap＝笔帽。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan为什么先划掉“Anna也想见你”，后来又重新写了相关信息？
2. Mum答应了什么、还没有答应什么？第六封信有没有寄出？

## 读句子

**He checks its cap before he puts it away.**

拆开看：He / checks its cap / before he puts it away.

他／检查笔帽／再把笔收好。
